title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Accepting Bankruptcy Applications of Enterprises Whose Repayment Obligations for Loans from International Financial Organizations and Foreign Governments Have Not Yet Been Fulfilled
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issues Concerning the Acceptance of Bankruptcy Applications of Enterprises That Have Borrowed from International Financial Organizations and Foreign Governments but Whose Repayment Obligations Have Not Yet Been Fulfilled

Fa [2009] No. 389

To: All High People's Courts of Provinces, Autonomous Regions, and Municipalities Directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region

Recently, some local people's courts have requested instructions from our court on whether to accept bankruptcy applications of enterprises that have borrowed from international financial organizations and foreign governments but whose repayment obligations have not yet been fulfilled. Upon deliberation, we hereby notify the relevant issues as follows, which shall be followed and implemented.

As of June 1, 2007, if an enterprise that has borrowed loans or on-lent loans from international financial organizations or foreign governments applies for bankruptcy or is applied for bankruptcy, the people's court shall accept the case in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China.

For the aforementioned enterprises that signed on-lending agreements before June 1, 2007, but whose repayment obligations have not yet been fulfilled, the provisions of Article 3 of the Supreme People's Court's Notice on Several Issues to Be Noted in the Trial of Enterprise Bankruptcy Cases by People's Courts (Fa Fa [1997] No. 2) and the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Notice on Issues to Be Noted in the Implementation of Article 3 of Document Fa Fa [1997] No. 2 (Fa Han [1998] No. 74) shall continue to apply.

December 3, 2009
